title: Road Markings Along the Road
whatItIs: White lines along the road divide traffic and warn of hazards. When the lines get longer and the gaps shorter, there is a hazard ahead.
keyFacts: A broken white line marks the centre of the road.
Longer lines with shorter gaps warn of a hazard: don't cross unless you can see the road is clear.

keyFacts.text: Where the line nearest you is solid, you MUST NOT cross or straddle it, except in the cases allowed.

keyFacts: You may cross it to pass a stationary vehicle, or to overtake a cyclist, horse or works vehicle at 10 mph or less.
Where the line nearest you is broken, you may cross to overtake if it's safe and you can finish in time.

onTheTest.question: There are double white lines and the one nearest you is solid. When may you cross it?
options: When the road ahead looks clear
onTheTest.why: The exceptions include passing a stationary vehicle, turning into a side road or property, and overtaking a cyclist, horse or works vehicle at 10 mph or less.

traps: 'Never' is wrong: the solid line has exceptions, such as passing a stationary vehicle.
The 10 mph exception is for cyclists, horses and road maintenance vehicles, not slow cars or lorries.
A hazard warning line isn't a ban, but don't overtake unless the road is clearly safe.
